source: GMCA Research Team, Unit Cost Database v3.0 (FINAL), updated autumn 2025 (published Nov 2025); workbook gmca-unit-cost-database-v3-0-final.xlsx
price_base: 2025/26 prices (column J 'Updated cost/saving' / column M; workbook Lookups!K10 = 2025/26, uprated by the workbook's GDP-deflator lookup from the source year in column I)

items.label: Universal Credit: single workless claimant, no children, entering full-time work - fiscal benefit
items.components: benefit savings + tax/NI (DWP benefit payments and operational costs £11,249.96 [E&E1.0.1] + income tax/employee and employer NIC/indirect tax £6,486.00 [E&E1.0.2])
items.source_ref: Sheet 'Employment & Economy', row 3, cost code E&E1.0, column H/J (fiscal value); subsidiaries rows 4-5 (E&E1.0.1, E&E1.0.2)
items.note: Source: DWP modelling (unpublished), RAG amber. Assumes 37 h/week at the 2025/26 National Living Wage (21+), privately renting at £1,332/month, one additional year in work. Comment gives a no-rent alternative of £12,867 fiscal, which suits younger claimants. Also includes reduced DWP operational costs and VAT/indirect tax, so it is slightly wider than benefits + direct tax/NI. Components sum to £17,735.96, a £0.23 rounding difference from the headline. Same row: economic value £26,297.40 (col M), social value £3,204.00 (col P). The workbook says fiscal values are transfers to exclude from public value; WP86 displacement sensitivity is 20% supply-side and 45% demand-side. Part-time alternative E&E1.1 = £6,685.18.

items.label: Employment and Support Allowance: workless claimant entering work - fiscal benefit (benefits + tax/NI, excluding NHS health element)
items.components: benefit savings + tax/NI (E&E3.0.1 benefits payments incl. HB and operational costs £12,820.20 + E&E3.0.2 income tax/NIC/indirect tax net of tax credits £2,649.30)
items.source_ref: Sheet 'Employment & Economy', rows 38-39, cost codes E&E3.0.1 + E&E3.0.2, column J (headline E&E3.0 row 37)
items.price_base: 2025/26 (uprated by the workbook from 2017/18 source values)
items.note: No UC health / LCW / LCWRA into-work entry exists in v3.0; the new UC entries E&E1.0-1.7 cover only jobseeker-type household scenarios, so this uses the legacy ESA entry. Source: DWP modelling (unpublished), 2017/18 prices, RAG amber. The 2017/18 constituents are £7,270 ESA, £1,942 HB and £442 operational costs (total £9,654), plus £968 income tax, £928 employer NIC, £790 employee NIC and £495 indirect tax, minus a £1,186 tax-credit offset (net £1,995). Adding the NHS improved-health element E&E3.0.3 (£1,552.39, from WP86 Appendix D, flagged 'use with caution') gives the headline E&E3.0 fiscal value of £17,021.90. The E&E3.0 economic value is £19,059.00 (col M).

items.label: Employment and Support Allowance: workless claimant entering work - headline fiscal benefit incl. NHS improved-health saving
items.components: benefit savings + tax/NI + NHS improved health (E&E3.0.1 + E&E3.0.2 + E&E3.0.3)
items.source_ref: Sheet 'Employment & Economy', row 37, cost code E&E3.0, column J
items.note: Headline ESA value; RAG amber. The NHS element comes from DWP WP86 and is uncertain.

items.label: Jobseeker's Allowance (legacy): workless claimant entering work - fiscal benefit (benefits + tax/NI, excluding NHS health element)
items.components: benefit savings + tax/NI (E&E2.0.1 benefits incl. HB and operational costs £9,927.89 + E&E2.0.2 income tax/NIC/indirect tax £6,103.34)
items.source_ref: Sheet 'Employment & Economy', rows 28-29, cost codes E&E2.0.1 + E&E2.0.2, column J (headline E&E2.0 row 27)
items.price_base: 2025/26 (uprated by the workbook from 2017/18 source values)
items.note: Cross-check for uc_jobseeker_into_work; it is on the same benefit+tax basis as health_claimant_into_work. The 2017/18 constituents are £4,000 JSA, £2,328 HB and £1,148 operational costs, plus £1,375 income tax, £1,244 employer NIC, £1,024 employee NIC and £1,016 indirect tax, minus a £63 tax-credit offset. Adding the NHS element E&E2.0.3 (£776.86) gives the headline E&E2.0 fiscal value of £16,808.09. Economic value is £23,133.20. Source: DWP modelling (unpublished), RAG amber.

items.label: NEET: average current fiscal cost per 18-24 year old NEET
items.components: benefit payments (worklessness + housing benefit, DWP £4,781.24 [E&E10.0.1]) + HMRC element £1,543.73 [E&E10.0.2]
items.source_ref: Sheet 'Employment & Economy', row 82, cost code E&E10.0, column J (fiscal)
items.note: Source: ACEVO Commission on Youth Unemployment (2012), 'Youth Unemployment: the crisis we cannot afford'; Coles et al 2010 is the source only for the lifetime entry E&E10.4. RAG red: a top-down national total divided by NEET numbers, old data, and no health or crime costs. This is the cost while the person is NEET. The HMRC element is internally inconsistent: the headline note says foregone tax/NI net of WTC/CTC, but the E&E10.0.2 note says it 'relates to payments of Working Tax Credits and Child Tax Credits'.

items.label: NEET: average current economic cost (lost earnings) per 18-24 year old NEET
items.components: lost earnings to the individual while NEET
items.source_ref: Sheet 'Employment & Economy', row 82, cost code E&E10.0, column M (economic)
items.note: ACEVO 2012; RAG red. Social value not quantified.

items.label: NEET: average current fiscal cost per 16-17 year old NEET
items.components: benefit payments (DWP); net HMRC element nil
items.source_ref: Sheet 'Employment & Economy', row 85, cost code E&E10.1, column J (economic value col M = £6,798.93)

items.label: NEET: average future annual fiscal cost per individual related to earlier NEET status - males
items.components: foregone tax/NI (HMRC £3,604.04, E&E10.2.1) + future workless benefit payments (DWP £722.98, E&E10.2.2)
items.source_ref: Sheet 'Employment & Economy', row 86, cost code E&E10.2, column J (economic col M = £10,360.35)
items.note: This is a scarring cost in later life, not the cost while NEET. ACEVO 2012; RAG red.

items.label: NEET: average future annual fiscal cost per individual related to earlier NEET status - females
items.components: foregone tax/NI (HMRC) + future workless benefit payments (DWP)
items.source_ref: Sheet 'Employment & Economy', row 89, cost code E&E10.3, column J (economic col M = £6,693.44)
items.note: This is a scarring cost in later life. ACEVO 2012; RAG red.

items.label: NEET (16-18): lifetime public finance cost - welfare payments (less pensions) + lost tax/NI
items.components: benefit payments + lost tax/NI over lifetime
items.source_ref: Sheet 'Employment & Economy', row 92, cost code E&E10.4, column J
items.note: Source: Coles et al 2010, 'Estimating the life-time cost of NEET: 16-18 year olds not in Education, Employment or Training' (University of York), p37 table 3.7. This is a case-study-based LIFETIME figure, not per year. RAG red.
